newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong runaway entrepreneurs start young.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong runaway entrepreneurs start young.

text.p: Two tiny Hong Kong runaways went on a five-day junk food spree which they funded by reselling used tin cans and waste paper.
Yip Ka-wai, aged nine, and Tong Hiu-fat, eight, disappeared last Wednesday sparking fears they had been kidnapped.
But the pair were found in a 24-hour convenience store on Monday having spent the intervening days playing in shopping malls, renting bicycles and sleeping rough.

The pair had about HK$20 (US$2.50) each in their pockets when they went missing but made enough cash to gorge themselves to their hearts content on chips, instant noodles and fizzy drinks, police said on Tuesday.
Kai-wai returned home with $40 ($5), the English-language South China Morning Post said. His relieved parents said the first thing on the agenda for the budding businessman was a bath.
"They were just two very naughty boys, but they were very switched on," the Post quoted a senior policeman as saying.
